summary: All three prior code-review BLOCKs (CR-001 error envelope, CR-002 request-scoped PII redaction, CR-003 money-guard exemption) are independently verified CLOSED by executing the code at HEAD, not by reading its comments. Two NEW BLOCKs found, both introduced by the remediation commits themselves: (1) the /metrics RED counter is keyed on the raw request path instead of the matched route template, giving unbounded attacker-controlled counter cardinality (500 unknown paths -> 500 permanent series, 37 KB /metrics body) and destroying per-route aggregation as soon as a path-param route lands; (2) the new global HTTPException handler discards exc.headers, so 405 responses lose the RFC-required Allow header and a future 401 loses its WWW-Authenticate challenge - a regression against the FastAPI default handler it replaced. Four of the six reviewer hypotheses supplied in the spawn prompt were refuted with evidence (contextvar non-unwind, bare asserts under -O, per-request Settings(), and the loggerDict-once gap for the common propagating case). E11-S1 and the Money type are clean; no file exceeds 300 lines and no function exceeds 24.

prior_blocks_verified.evidence: backend/src/api/errors.py:131-136 registers AppError, StarletteHTTPException, RequestValidationError and Exception. Live probe of create_app() under TestClient(raise_server_exceptions=False) with injected routes returned the exact frozen {error,detail,context} shape at application/json for 404 ({"error":"NotFound","detail":"Not Found","context":{}}), 405, 401, 403, 409, 422 body-validation ({"error":"ValidationError","detail":"request validation failed","context":{"field":"body.n"}}), an AppError subclass ({"error":"PolicyViolationException",...}) and an unhandled RuntimeError (500 -> {"error":"InternalServerError","detail":"internal server error","context":{}} with the exception message, absolute path and SQL all absent). Key names and nesting match specs/design/api-contracts.md:26-27.
prior_blocks_verified.residual: The same handler drops exc.headers - filed as new BLOCK CR2-002, not a reopening of CR-001.

prior_blocks_verified.evidence: backend/src/config/logging.py:44 holds a mutable set in the contextvar and register_sensitive (:74-81) mutates it in place; backend/src/api/middleware.py:89 opens the scope and :96-102 logs the exception before re-raising. Tested the FastAPI sync-handler-in-threadpool case explicitly: a `def` handler registering ABCDE1234F/123456789012 then raising produced `RuntimeError: boom pan=[REDACTED] aadhaar=[REDACTED]` with "request_id": "rid-sync_fail". The traceback frames confirm the real threadpool path was taken (anyio/_backends/_asyncio.py:1100 `result = context.run(func, *args)`), so the in-place mutation genuinely survives the context copy as the comment claims. Across sync-fail, async-fail and sync-success: 0 leaking lines, 0 lines with a wrong or empty request_id. Both halves of the finding (unredacted PII AND empty request_id) are closed.
prior_blocks_verified.residual: Latent silent no-op if register_sensitive is ever called with no scope open (CR2-W16); lru_cache retains PII values process-globally (CR2-W09). Neither reopens CR-002.

prior_blocks_verified.evidence: backend/tests/architecture/test_no_float_money.py:82-86 now reads `if is_division and getattr(node, 'lineno', None) in exempt: continue` before `if is_float_call or is_math_attr or is_float_literal or is_division: count += 1`, so the `continue` is gated on is_division and the marker exempts exactly one category. The regression test test_division_exemption_does_not_silence_other_float_categories (:272-297) asserts _count_float_usages > 0 for a marked line carrying float(...), a marked line carrying `+ 0.5`, and a marked `import math` - all three returned 0 under the pre-fix whole-line continue. 88 backend tests pass.

hypotheses_assessed.hypothesis: _install_redaction_filter_everywhere iterates loggerDict once; later loggers get no filter
hypotheses_assessed.evidence: Refuted for the common case: the RedactionFilter on the root StreamHandler (logging.py:199) applies to every record reaching it, so a logger created after configure_logging that propagates IS covered - verified by a logging.getLogger('biz') created inside a request handler whose PAN was scrubbed on root-handler output. Confirmed real only for a post-startup logger with propagate=False and its own handler: probe logging.getLogger('late.thirdparty') had RedactionFilter on neither the logger nor its handler.

hypotheses_assessed.hypothesis: middleware.py:102 leaking both contextvars risks cross-request bleed
hypotheses_assessed.evidence: One task context per request cycle under both uvicorn and TestClient, so the set() dies with the task (PEP 567). Probed: after a 500 that registered a PAN, the next request saw {"vals": [], "rid": "<fresh id>"} and the module-level contextvar read back None / ''. The non-unwind is also what keeps the server's own traceback line scrubbed.

hypotheses_assessed.hypothesis: module-level globals in platform/routes.py and the Counter in middleware.py are a testability/concurrency defect
hypotheses_assessed.outcome: confirmed as a defect, but the severity is in the label not the globalness
hypotheses_assessed.evidence: Counter increments run only on the event-loop thread, so no thread-safety issue. State is however shared across every create_app() in a process, which is why test_health_probe.py must call reset_database_probe() inline.

hypotheses_assessed.hypothesis: bare assert isinstance(...) narrowing is stripped under python -O
hypotheses_assessed.evidence: Handler bodies read attributes only (exc.status_code, exc.error, exc.message, exc.context, exc.errors()) and Starlette dispatches by exception type, so stripping the assert removes type narrowing, not a guard.

hypotheses_assessed.hypothesis: get_health constructs Settings() on every request
hypotheses_assessed.evidence: Measured 0.073 ms per construction (1000 in 73 ms) against a 500 ms p95 SLO; SettingsConfigDict names no env_file so there is no per-request disk read.

hypotheses_assessed.hypothesis: the three reset_* functions exist only for tests
hypotheses_assessed.evidence: reset_database_probe (routes.py:44) and reset_request_counters (middleware.py:57) have no production caller; grep shows references only from tests.

findings.title: /metrics RED counter keyed on the raw request path: unbounded attacker-controlled cardinality and broken route aggregation
findings.description: The counter key comes from scope.get('path') captured at middleware.py:91 - the literal request path, not the matched route template - and _request_counts (middleware.py:49) has no bound and no eviction. Probed against the real app: 500 requests to /random-path-0..499 produced 500 permanent counter series and a 36,980-byte /metrics body. Any client can therefore add an unbounded number of permanent series through a public, unauthenticated endpoint. Separately, specs/design/api-contracts.md:315 requires metrics 'labelled method, route, status' and routes.py:72 promises the same; once a path-param route lands (/applications/{application_id}, E8-S1 in the next group) every application id becomes its own series and the runtime-SLO sensor can no longer compute a per-route p95 or error rate. The 404 case already triggers it today.
findings.remediation: Resolve the label lazily inside send_with_correlation_id from the matched route template, which the router has populated by the time http.response.start is sent (verified: path=/apps/123 -> route=/apps/{app_id}), and collapse unmatched paths to one constant: `route = getattr(scope.get('route'), 'path', None) or '<unmatched>'`. Keep the raw path for the access-log line if wanted; only the counter key must be bounded. Add a test asserting two requests to /apps/{id} with different ids produce one series.

findings.title: New global HTTPException handler discards exc.headers: 405 loses Allow, 401 loses WWW-Authenticate
findings.description: handle_http_error builds the envelope via _envelope(...) and never forwards exc.headers. FastAPI's default http_exception_handler - the handler this one replaces - does headers=getattr(exc, 'headers', None), so the diff regressed header behaviour while fixing the body. Probed: POST /health returns 405 with headers {content-length, content-type, x-request-id} and Allow: None, violating RFC 9110 s15.5.6; HTTPException(401, headers={'WWW-Authenticate': 'Bearer'}) returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: None. Reachable today for every wrong-method request. Reachable next group because decision D-F makes require_roles the single auth enforcement point and api-contracts.md:26-29 specifies '401 no or invalid token'; a Bearer challenge will be swallowed and no current test would notice, since every error test asserts only on the body.
findings.remediation: Add a headers parameter to _envelope and pass it through JSONResponse, then call `_envelope(exc.status_code, name, str(exc.detail), headers=getattr(exc, 'headers', None))` in handle_http_error. Add one assertion that POST /health returns 405 carrying an Allow header.

findings.title: Database probe exception swallowed with no log line
findings.description: `except Exception: return 'down'` discards the cause entirely - no log, no exc_info. Returning 'down' is the correct behaviour, but this is the platform-observability story and an operator cannot distinguish a connection refusal from a permission error or a timeout.
findings.remediation: Log at WARNING with exc_info=True before returning 'down'.

findings.title: RedactionFilter installed on loggerDict only once, so 'everywhere' cannot hold
findings.description: The per-logger install is a snapshot taken at configure time. A logger created afterwards that sets propagate=False and installs its own handler is covered by neither the logger filter nor the root handler filter - probed: logging.getLogger('late.thirdparty') plus its own StreamHandler had RedactionFilter on neither. The common propagating case IS covered by the root-handler filter, so there is no PII leak today; the function's name promises a guarantee it cannot deliver, and the per-logger installs otherwise duplicate the handler filter.
findings.remediation: Either rely solely on the root-handler filter and delete/rename this function, or move redaction into a LogRecord factory so loggers created later are covered too.

findings.title: Both AC2 'every logger has the filter' tests pass by construction
findings.description: test_redaction_filter_installed_on_every_configured_logger (:43-65) and test_redaction_filter_covers_every_logger_under_the_real_server_config (:190-220) each call create_app()/configure_logging() and then enumerate logging.root.manager.loggerDict - i.e. they enumerate exactly the set the implementation just iterated, so they cannot fail. They restate _install_redaction_filter_everywhere rather than asserting a durable property, and the pytest.raises(AssertionError) on a hand-built logging.Logger (:63-65) proves the local helper, not the system.
findings.remediation: Assert the behaviour instead: create a logger AFTER configure_logging, emit a registered sensitive value through it, and assert the sink shows [REDACTED].

findings.title: dictConfig(uvicorn LOGGING_CONFIG) applied globally with no teardown, in two duplicated places
findings.description: Also at backend/tests/unit/test_correlation_id.py:62. Both apply logging.config.dictConfig(uvicorn.config.LOGGING_CONFIG) and never restore the previous configuration, mutating process-wide logging for the remainder of the session and making the suite order-dependent. The two blocks are near-identical.
findings.remediation: Extract one fixture that snapshots and restores logging configuration in a finally block, and use it from both tests.

findings.title: Health-probe test mutates a module global without try/finally
findings.description: register_database_probe(lambda: False) is undone only by the reset_database_probe() call on the last line of the test body (:68). A failing assertion in between leaves the failing probe registered, silently changing /health for every later test in the session.
findings.remediation: Move the registration into a fixture that resets in finally, or wrap the body in try/finally.

findings.title: Inbound X-Request-ID reflected with no validation or length cap
findings.description: The header is taken verbatim, echoed into the response header and written into every JSON log line for the request. Probed: a 5,000-character X-Request-ID is echoed back at full length and appears in each log line. json.dumps prevents log injection, but this is unbounded attacker-controlled log volume and response-header size.
findings.remediation: Cap the accepted length (e.g. 128 chars) and regenerate the id when the inbound value is over the cap or contains characters outside an allowed token set.

findings.title: Module-level mutable globals plus reset_* functions that exist only for tests
findings.description: Also backend/src/api/middleware.py:49,57. Two module-level globals mutated via `global` statements, plus reset_database_probe (routes.py:44) and reset_request_counters (middleware.py:57) which have no production caller - production API shaped by test needs. The state is shared across every create_app() in a process, so app instances are not isolated; test_health_probe.py:58-68 has to undo it by hand.
findings.remediation: Hold the probe and the counters on the app instance (app.state) or in an injected registry object, so each app is isolated and both reset_* functions can be deleted.

findings.title: Importing src.api.app reconfigures global logging as a side effect
findings.description: Module-level `app = create_app()` runs Settings() and configure_logging(), which calls root.handlers.clear() (logging.py:202). Merely importing src.api.app destroys any handler the host process had installed. backend/tests/conftest.py:36-39 documents the workaround: log_capture must depend on the client fixture so it attaches after the handler reset.
findings.remediation: Move the module-level construction behind the ASGI entrypoint (or guard it), so importing the module has no global effect.

findings.title: lru_cache keyed on the raw sensitive value retains PII process-globally
findings.description: @lru_cache(maxsize=256) on _redaction_pattern is keyed by the sensitive value itself, so up to 256 PANs/Aadhaars remain resident in a process-global cache long after the request scope that registered them has ended - the opposite of the request-scoped lifetime the rest of the module is built around.
findings.remediation: Key the cache on a digest of the value, or move the compiled-pattern cache into the request-scoped structure so it dies with the scope.

findings.title: Values shorter than 6 characters are silently never redacted
findings.description: _scrub skips any value shorter than _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH = 6 with a bare `continue`. register_sensitive('12345') returns normally and the caller has no way to learn the value will never be scrubbed. The threshold itself is sound; the silence is the defect.
findings.remediation: Log once at WARNING when a registered value is below the threshold, or have register_sensitive report which values it accepted.

findings.title: MoneyField / serializers.py has no behavioural test at all
findings.description: The only reference from the suite is backend/tests/architecture/test_no_float_money.py:26,100, which reads the file as text for the AST float scan. specs/design/architecture.md decision D-G names this 'the ONE module' converting Money to and from the wire and every later money field depends on it. I probed it through a real FastAPI route and it is correct ('100.00' round-trips as a quoted string; 100, 100.5, 'abc' and null each produce a 422 rather than a 500, because InvalidMoneyAmountError subclasses ValueError) - but no test guards any of that.
findings.remediation: Add a round-trip test through a route using MoneyField: a valid quoted 2dp string in and out, plus a JSON number and a non-numeric string each asserting 422.

findings.title: /health returns database/status values absent from the frozen contract, and serves 'degraded' with HTTP 200
findings.description: The probe returns database: 'unconfigured' and can return status: 'degraded'. Neither value appears in specs/design/api-contracts.md:314 ({"status":"ok","database":"ok","version":"..."}), while specs/design/amendments/group-a-gate-remediation.md states the contract is deliberately NOT amended because 'it is the authoritative frozen side, so the code changes to match it, not the reverse' - so the code still does not match the side the amendment calls authoritative. test_health_reports_the_contract_shape asserts only the key set, not the values. Separately, status:'degraded' is served with HTTP 200, so an orchestrator liveness probe reading only the status code never sees the degradation.
findings.remediation: Amend api-contracts.md to enumerate the three database values (ok | down | unconfigured) and the two status values, or return a non-2xx when status is 'degraded'. Pick one and make the test assert the values, not just the keys.

findings.title: Production docstrings narrate prior-defect history instead of the current design
findings.description: About 14 sites across logging.py, middleware.py, errors.py, platform/routes.py and five test files carry commit-log content in source: 'It previously returned {"status": "ok"} alone' (routes.py:7), 'The gate measured 0.58 -> 314 ms and 199 s at length 40' (test_log_redaction.py:236), 'Five reviewers found this independently and it was demonstrated live' (:262), 'api-contracts.md is frozen, so the code is the stale side' (test_health_probe.py:33), 'went unreported' (test_no_float_money.py:85), 'it reported 100% while the running server had...' (test_log_redaction.py:196). This will be stale within one story and tells a future reader about a bug that no longer exists rather than about the invariant being protected.
findings.remediation: Keep the design rationale (e.g. 'separator-bearing values are matched literally to avoid quantifier/literal ambiguity'); delete the gate archaeology, the reviewer counts and the measured timings - those belong in the commit message and this review.

findings.title: frontend/package-lock.json is gitignored, so installs are not reproducible
findings.description: The lockfile exists on disk (157 KB) but .gitignore:49 excludes it and git ls-files confirms it is untracked. Every dependency in frontend/package.json:13-31 is a caret range, so a fresh install on another machine or in CI resolves different versions than the ones the 18 passing frontend tests were run against. For an application (not a published library) the lockfile belongs in git.
findings.remediation: Remove the package-lock.json entry from .gitignore and commit frontend/package-lock.json.

findings.title: Money.multiply throws a raw DecimalError instead of the module's typed error
findings.description: multiply builds `new Decimal(scalar)` outside toQuantizedDecimal, so an invalid numeric string throws decimal.js's own DecimalError rather than InvalidMoneyAmountError - inconsistent with fromWire (:46), which is the error contract the module documents and the test suite asserts (money.test.ts:53-55).
findings.remediation: Route the scalar through the same try/catch as toQuantizedDecimal so every invalid input surfaces as InvalidMoneyAmountError; add one test.

findings.title: register_sensitive is a silent no-op when no redaction scope is open
findings.description: _current_values() creates and set()s a scope-less set when the contextvar holds None. Inside a threadpool context copy that set() is discarded on return, so register_sensitive called outside a middleware-opened scope silently registers nothing - the same failure mode CR-002 described, minus the middleware. Every production path opens the scope today, so this is latent rather than live.
findings.remediation: Raise (or log at WARNING) when no scope is bound, instead of fabricating one that may be discarded.

findings.title: Deliberate contextvar non-unwind on the failure path is sound
findings.description: Verified no cross-request bleed: one task context per request cycle means the set() dies with the task. After a 500 that registered a PAN, the next request saw an empty set and a fresh request id, and the module-level contextvar read back None/''.
findings.remediation: Optional: state the assumption the design rests on (one task context per request cycle) in the docstring, since that is what a future reader must re-check if the mount point changes.

findings.title: assert isinstance narrowing is safe under python -O
findings.description: Also :105 and :116. Stripping the asserts removes type narrowing, not a guard: the bodies only read attributes and Starlette dispatches by exception type.
findings.remediation: Optional: use typing.cast to express the narrowing without relying on a statement that can be compiled out.

findings.title: Settings() per /health request is redundant but negligible
findings.description: Measured 0.073 ms per construction (1000 in 73 ms) against a 500 ms p95 SLO, and SettingsConfigDict names no env_file so there is no per-request disk read. The factory already builds a Settings at app.py:33.
findings.remediation: Optional: pass version in from the factory or memoise with functools.lru_cache.

findings.title: 422 envelope reports only the first validation error
findings.description: field is built from errors[0]['loc'] only. Adequate for the contract as written; the E4/E5 application-submission forms will likely want every offending field.
findings.remediation: Revisit when the first multi-field form endpoint lands; no change needed for group A.

findings.title: 405 maps to the error name 'HTTPError', outside the contract vocabulary
findings.description: _STATUS_ERROR_NAMES has no 405 entry, so the fallback 'HTTPError' is emitted. api-contracts.md:28-29 enumerates 401/403/404/409/422 only, so a client switching on the error name sees an undocumented value.
findings.remediation: Add 405: 'MethodNotAllowed' to _STATUS_ERROR_NAMES, or document the fallback in the contract.

findings.title: Missing blank lines between top-level test functions
findings.description: Also :45, :76, :109; test_error_envelope.py:32,63; test_log_redaction.py:43,66,98. Top-level defs run together with no separating blank line, unlike every production module in the diff. ruff does not select E301/E302 in this project, so the gate cannot see the drift.
findings.remediation: Add the two blank lines, or enable E301/E302 in the ruff configuration.

findings.title: No coverage tooling in the backend, so the project's 80% floor is unmeasured
findings.description: Out of the diff scope, but noted because pytest --cov errors with 'unrecognized arguments' - pytest-cov is not installed. CLAUDE.md states a 100% meaningful-coverage target with an 80% floor, and CR2-W11 (serializers.py with zero behavioural tests) is exactly what such a floor would have caught.
findings.remediation: Add pytest-cov and a coverage floor to the backend dev dependencies in a separate change.

findings.title: decimal.js default precision (20) differs from Python's decimal context (28)
findings.description: Intermediate products in multiply are computed at 20 significant digits on the frontend and 28 on the backend. The rounding mode does match - I verified -45.005 quantizes to -45.01 on both sides, so ROUND_HALF_UP is away-from-zero in both runtimes. The precision gap can only bite at magnitudes far beyond any loan principal, but it is an unstated cross-runtime assumption behind decision D-G.
findings.remediation: Optional: set Decimal.set({ precision: 28 }) in the frontend money module so both sides share one intermediate precision.
